panels.title: Servers
panels.description: Every tenant ever created, published or not.

panels.title: Published
panels.description: Servers whose page is publicly live. The gap between this and Servers is people who signed up but never finished.

panels.title: Active (30d)
panels.description: Servers that uploaded in the last 30 days. This is the retention number that matters.

panels.title: Owners
panels.description: Discord accounts that have signed in. Synthetic partner logins are not counted.

panels.title: New owners (30d)
panels.description: Accounts created in the last 30 days. Read it next to Servers - owners without servers means people sign in and stop.

panels.title: Players indexed
panels.description: Across every live build. This is the audience, not the customer count.

panels.title: Players (live)
panels.description: Players counted by the build currently live on each server. Lower than Players indexed when an older build still holds rows for servers that shrank.

panels.title: Player-hours
panels.description: Total playtime represented on the platform.

panels.title: Growth
panels.description: Gauges over time. Flat published-vs-total means people are signing up and stalling before publishing — look at the funnel below.

panels.title: Publish rate
panels.description: Of everyone who created a server, how many actually published. Low means onboarding is losing people.

panels.title: 30d retention
panels.description: Of published servers, how many uploaded recently. For an annual product a low number here is expected outside December.

panels.title: Traffic — how much is it being looked at?
Player lookups 24h
panels.description: A player document actually read — someone opened a specific person's Wrapped.

panels.title: Link previews 24h
panels.description: OG images served. Each one means somebody's link was unfurled in Discord — the closest signal we have to sharing.

panels.title: Views and shares
panels.description: Rolling 24h windows sampled every scrape. Link previews rising faster than page views means the thing is spreading in Discord before people click through.

panels.title: 30-day windows
panels.description: Slower-moving view of the same. Better for spotting a trend than a spike.

panels.title: Page views by kind
panels.description: Server pages are the front door; player pages are the thing people share. If server views climb and player views do not, the story is not being reached.

panels.title: Player lookups: hit vs miss
panels.description: A miss is somebody asking for a player the live build has no row for - a name typo, a renamed account, or somebody who never played.

panels.title: Lookup miss rate (24h)
panels.description: Share of player lookups that found nothing. A rising miss rate usually means name changes are outrunning the usercache.

panels.title: Head cache ratio (24h)
panels.description: Player heads are fetched once and cached forever, so this should climb towards 1 and stay there. A drop means the head cache is being missed and Mojang is being called instead.

panels.title: Name lookups by tier (30d)
panels.description: Where uuid to name answers came from: KV, then the D1 usercache, then Mojang. Mojang should be the thin slice - it is the only tier that can rate-limit us.

panels.title: Name lookups by tier
panels.description: The same three tiers over time. A step change in the Mojang slice is worth chasing before it turns into throttling.

panels.title: Pipeline health — did the uploads actually become pages?
Snapshots 24h
panels.description: Uploads accepted in the last day, straight from D1. Compare with Uploads 24h from the event stream - a gap means events are being dropped, not uploads.

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: ALERT ON THIS. A failed build means somebody's upload silently never became a page, and they will not find out on their own.

panels.title: Queued
panels.description: Snapshots accepted and waiting for the build queue. Always emitted, so 0 means idle, not broken.

panels.title: Building
panels.description: Should be near zero outside a build. Stuck here means a build died without marking itself failed.

panels.title: Stuck (>1h)
panels.description: Snapshots still marked building an hour after they arrived. Anything but 0 is a build that died without writing its failure back.

panels.title: Snapshots by state
panels.description: Cumulative. A growing 'failed' band is the thing to catch early.

panels.title: Ingest and build throughput
panels.description: These should track each other. Builds lagging uploads means the queue is backing up.

panels.title: Uploads by source (30d)
panels.description: Which door uploads come through: the browser wizard, the shell client, or a hosting panel. Tells you which client to fix first when uploads stall.

panels.title: Builds: ok vs failed (30d)
panels.description: Every failed build is somebody whose upload silently never became a page.

panels.title: Build failure rate (30d)
panels.description: Failed builds as a share of all builds. Alert on any sustained rise - the owner will not find out on their own.

panels.title: Cost — what is this actually costing?
Est. monthly
panels.description: ESTIMATE from our own counters against a rate table in src/api/metrics.js. Cloudflare's invoice is authoritative — this exists to spot a trend before the invoice arrives.

panels.title: OG spend (30d)
panels.description: Cost of rendering preview images. Each render is ~250ms CPU; each cache hit is free.

panels.title: Storage
panels.description: R2 usage. First 10 GB free, then $0.015/GB-month. Egress is always free.

panels.title: CPU-ms (30d)
panels.description: 30 million included on the $5 plan. At ~2.4s per build that is ~12,500 builds a month.

panels.title: Requests (30d)
panels.description: 10 million included on the $5 plan.

panels.title: OG cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of link previews served straight from R2. Each cached one is free; each render is ~250 ms of CPU. Should sit near 1 - if it falls, something is changing the card's R2 key.

panels.title: Preview images: cached vs rendered
panels.description: Rendered images cost money; cached ones do not.

panels.title: Estimated spend over time
panels.description: Watch the shape, not the number. A step change means something started rendering that used to be cached.

panels.title: Java vs Bedrock
panels.description: Bedrock players arrive through Geyser with a Floodgate UUID and a prefixed name.

panels.title: Players indexed
panels.description: Steps up when a server uploads. Drops mean a server was deleted or rebuilt smaller.

panels.title: Average players per active server
panels.description: Tells you whether you are attracting big servers or small ones.

panels.title: Partners
panels.description: Hosting companies registered against /v1/host.

panels.title: Active
panels.description: Partners that can still create servers and push snapshots.

panels.title: Paused
panels.description: Reversibly suspended: their /v1/host calls are refused, nothing else changes.

panels.title: Revoked
panels.description: One-way. Kept only so the audit log still reads.

panels.title: Partner-owned servers
panels.description: Servers created through a partner, claimed or not. The rest were created by hand.

panels.title: Open claims
panels.description: Claim links issued and not yet opened. These expire - a number that only grows means partners are handing out links nobody follows.

panels.title: Partner estate
panels.description: Servers a partner created against claim links still outstanding. The gap between them is how much of the estate is still unowned.

panels.title: Partners by state
panels.description: Active, paused, revoked.

panels.title: Analytics pipeline
panels.description: 1 when the Analytics Engine query behind every event metric succeeded on the last scrape, 0 when it failed. If this reads BROKEN, check CF_ACCOUNT_ID and CF_ANALYTICS_TOKEN - the event panels are showing zeros, not truth.

panels.title: Raw snapshots held
panels.description: Uploads kept in R2 for rebuilds. Grows with every upload; the only thing here that grows without bound.

panels.title: Usercache entries
panels.description: uuid to name pairs held in D1 forever. This is the tier that keeps Mojang out of the request path, so it should only ever grow.

panels.title: Name lookups (24h)
panels.description: Total uuid to name resolutions across all three tiers.

panels.title: Heads served (30d)
panels.description: Player head images served, cached and fetched together.
